description: agro run services. ADR #1575 (Accepted) sequences step 2 (a per-worker service sidecar from a project declaration) and step 3 (a `/delegate` rule). Step 1 shipped in #1580: `EphemeralExecutionTarget` and `agro run`. Facts: `agro run` reads `agro.json` at the git toplevel for `image.ref` (`.agro/cli/src/commands/run.ts`). Parallel workers in the earlier agro-console tasks shared one `postgres` container and created throwaway databases by hand.

userStories.title: The run section of agro.json
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want run services in `agro.json` so that `agro run` starts the declared services for each command.
acceptanceCriteria: `AgroConfig` in `.agro/cli/src/lib/agro-config.ts` has an optional `run` section with `services` and `env`.
`run.services` maps a service name to an object with a required string `image`, an optional string map `env`, and an optional string `ready`.
`run.env` is an optional string map.
The validator rejects three inputs: a service name outside the DNS label format, a missing `image`, and a non-string value in `env`. Each error message names the field path.
Tests in `.agro/cli/src/lib/__tests__/agro-config.test.ts` cover each accepted shape and each rejection.
`pnpm typecheck` exits 0, and `pnpm test` shows no new failure against `evidence/baseline.md`.

userStories.title: agro run starts and removes the services
userStories.description: As a worker, I want `agro run` to give each command its own services so that parallel workers share no database.
acceptanceCriteria: When `run.services` is not empty, `agro run` creates a Docker network `agro-run-<id>` with a unique `<id>` for each invocation.
`agro run` starts each service with `docker run -d --rm` on that network, with the service name as its network alias and with the service `env`.
When a service has `ready`, `agro run` runs the `ready` command in the service container once per second. After 60 seconds without success, `agro run` exits 1 and names the service.
The command container joins the network and receives `run.env`.
After the command exits, and also after a failure, `agro run` removes each service container and the network.
When `run.services` is empty or absent, the `docker` argument vector of `agro run` does not change.
Tests assert the exact `docker` argument vectors and the removal order through a fake runner.
`pnpm typecheck` exits 0, and `pnpm test` shows no new failure against the baseline.

userStories.title: Delegate verifies through agro run
userStories.description: As an advisor, I want `/delegate` to run verification through `agro run` when the host has it so that verification does not depend on host drift.
acceptanceCriteria: `.agro/skills/delegate/SKILL.md` holds a rule for the `host` execution location. When `agro --help` lists `agro run`, the baseline, the worker verification, and the advisor acceptance commands run as `agro run -- <command>`.
The rule names the fallback: without `agro run`, or in a sandbox, the commands run directly.
`bash .agro/skills/ste/scripts/ste-check.sh .agro/skills/delegate/SKILL.md` reports no new finding on the changed lines.

userStories.title: Documentation and changelog
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the run section in the docs and the changelog so that a project can declare services.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/lifecycle-commands.md` describes `run.services` and `run.env` in the `agro run` section, with one `postgres` example.
`CHANGELOG.md` holds one entry under `## [Unreleased]` that links the task issue.

userStories.title: Validation
userStories.description: As the operator, I want proof that services start, isolate, and clean up so that ADR #1575 step 2 meets its validation rule.
acceptanceCriteria: `.agro/tasks/agro-run-services/evidence/manual-review.md` records a scratch repository whose `agro.json` declares a `postgres` service with a `ready` command, and an `agro run` command that connects to `postgres:5432`.
Two `agro run` invocations run at the same time with different networks and different service containers, and each one reaches its own database.
After both runs, `docker ps -a` and `docker network ls` show no `agro-run-` container or network.
The run deletes the scratch repository at the end.
